superseded_numeric_implementation.scope: scalar numerator divided by separately accumulated alpha followed by a 16-epsilon admissibility check

diagnosis.mathematical_invariant: 0 <= sum_i(W_i*v_i)/sum_i(W_i) <= 1 for binary v_i and nonnegative W_i
diagnosis.numeric_failure: the scalar numerator and geometric alpha are accumulated through different FP32 output channels, so their independently rounded values need not preserve numerator<=denominator near weak support
diagnosis.why_threshold_relaxation_is_rejected: a larger scene-derived epsilon would be an avoidable data-dependent numeric constant and would not restore the algebraic invariant

primitive_channels: v_i=1[source reference responsibility weight is positive]
implementation_correction.render: render both channels in one unnormalized Gaussian feature-compositor call with contribution_gamma=1
implementation_correction.coverage: FP64 visible_mass/denominator when denominator>0, cast once to FP32; exact-zero denominator is unsupported background with exact-zero coverage
implementation_correction.postcondition: coverage must be finite and exactly within [0,1] without clipping
implementation_correction.scalar_alpha_diagnostic: the renderer alpha map may be retained only as a diagnostic and cannot define the corrected denominator

equivalence_argument.exact_arithmetic: sum_i(W_i*v_i)+sum_i(W_i*(1-v_i))=sum_i(W_i), hence paired coverage equals the registered alpha-normalized scalar coverage
equivalence_argument.support_semantics: exact-zero denominator is unsupported background and receives zero; every strictly positive paired denominator uses the FP64 ratio

verification_before_promotion: fail closed on negative or non-finite paired masses
require corrected coverage in [0,1] for every frozen target frame
record maximum absolute difference from the legacy scalar-alpha coverage on pixels where the legacy value is within its original 16-epsilon admissibility interval
seal every coverage, quantile, threshold and continuous-margin array before any target mask access
